title: Police emergency response team to test stun guns
article: The Saskatoon Police Service may add the Taser stun gun to its arsenal this year.
The department has requested funding for two of the weapons in its latest budget, which must be approved by the Saskatoon police commission and city council.
The Saskatchewan Police Commission has approved the use of stun guns by municipal police forces.
Last year, a coroner's jury looking into the death of Saskatoon resident Keldon McMillan recommended city police examine the possibility of using stun guns.

McMillan, 33, died after being shot by police in a field off of Highway 41 about seven kilometres south of Wakaw. The shooting, which took place May 20, 2001, came after a high-speed chase involving city police and RCMP. McMillan was threatening to shoot officers with a handgun.

Acting Insp. Keith Atkinson, the spokesperson for city police, said the department's emergency response team will use the weapon on a trial basis if funding is approved. He said the guns cost less than $1,000 each.
The RCMP's emergency response team and Regina city police are already using stun guns. The weapon is used by many police forces across Canada.
"It gives another non-lethal weapon," said Atkinson.
"It's always better if we can use non-lethal force."

Stun guns have a pulsating, 50,000-volt electrical current that's delivered through two probes. The electrical current overpowers the body's normal electrical signals in the nervous system. The guns do not cause permanent damage.
Atkinson said a stun gun would not have made a difference in the McMillan case because officers were too far away to use the weapon.
RCMP spokesperson Heather Russell said the Mounties now deploy 12 Tasers with their riot squad and two with their emergency response team.
This year the RCMP plans to deploy another 30 Tasers at busy detachments. The stun guns will be used by officers escorting prisoners and in holding cells.
The RCMP have found the stun gun to be effective "to varying degrees," said Russell.

"It depends on conditions, factors and circumstances. It's like any other tool in your tool kit. It's not applicable in some cases. For instance, you would never use a Taser on someone with a gun. It causes your muscles to contract. Do you want that to happen to someone using a firearm?"
